steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: Muslims believe that physical death is not the end — there is an afterlife (akhirah). After death, the soul is questioned in the grave by Munkar and Nakir, and on the Day of Judgement (Yawm al-Din), all people will be resurrected and judged by Allah.

steps.title: Exam Tip
steps.body: Belief in akhirah is one of the Six Articles of Faith. Without it, the whole Islamic moral framework would collapse — there would be no ultimate justice and no reason to follow Allah's commands if this life is all there is.

steps.title: RS Exam Tips — Akhirah: Life After Death
steps.body: 1. For Akhirah: Life After Death questions, always include specific scriptural or source references where relevant 2. Explain both religious and non-religious viewpoints 3. Use specialist vocabulary precisely (e.g. terms from the specification) 4. Evaluate by analysing strengths and weaknesses of different views before reaching your conclusion 5. Link your discussion of Akhirah: Life After Death to its real-world impact on believers and society

steps.title: UK Context
steps.body: The Islamic funeral ritual reflects belief in akhirah: the body is washed, wrapped in a simple white shroud and buried facing Makkah as quickly as possible. Mourners recite the Shahadah and pray for the deceased’s forgiveness. In the UK, Muslim burials must comply with both Islamic law (which requires burial, not cremation) and UK cemetery regulations.

steps.title: Try it yourself

steps.title: Exam tips
steps.body: Always refer to specific sources of authority (scripture, sacred texts, religious leaders) Explain contrasting beliefs — different views within and between traditions Use key terminology precisely (e.g. tawhid, atonement, sanctity of life) For 12-mark evaluation questions, consider both sides before reaching a justified conclusion Link beliefs to their impact on individuals, communities and society Acknowledge diversity — no religious tradition has a single, uniform view
